title: World Cup 2026
description: Test your knowledge of the 2026 FIFA World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

questions.prompt: How many teams participated in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, marking the first expansion to this format?
questions.explanation: The 2026 World Cup expanded to 48 teams, up from the 32-team format used since 1998.

questions.prompt: Which three countries co-hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: The United States, Canada, and Mexico co-hosted the 2026 World Cup — the first tournament with three host nations.

questions.prompt: Which stadium hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final?
questions.explanation: MetLife Stadium in New Jersey hosted the 2026 World Cup Final.

questions.prompt: Which historic venue hosted matches at both the 1970 and 2026 FIFA World Cups?
questions.explanation: Estadio Azteca in Mexico City hosted games in 1970, 1986, and again in 2026, making it the only stadium to host matches at three World Cups.

questions.prompt: In the new 48-team group stage format, how many teams advanced from each group of three?
choices: All three plus best third-place sides
questions.explanation: The 2026 World Cup used 16 groups of three teams, with the top two from each group advancing to a 32-team knockout round.

questions.prompt: Which confederation qualified the most teams for the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: UEFA received 16 spots in the expanded 48-team tournament, the largest allocation of any confederation.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many cities across the three host nations staged 2026 World Cup matches?
questions.explanation: The tournament spanned 16 host cities: 11 in the United States, 2 in Canada, and 3 in Mexico.

questions.prompt: Which Canadian city hosted group-stage matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Both Toronto (BMO Field) and Vancouver (BC Place) hosted 2026 World Cup group-stage matches for Canada.
